goal: One focused hour on the alternating centre trace. Given the proved constraints D1-D5, which candidate invariant or forced-tail lemma is the best next falsification or symbolic step towards excluding an eventually alternating centre trace for a nonzero finitely supported Rule 30 row? Excluding period 2 is a PARTIAL result: every period at least 3 would remain open. Do not begin a days-long classification.
settled: D1: if the centre alternates and c_t=1 then a(t,-1)=1. The OR latches; independent of the right half.
D2: if the centre alternates and c_t=0 then a(t,-1)=1 XOR a(t,1).
D3: a(t,-2) = a(t+1,1) when c_t=1 and = a(t,1) when c_t=0. Column -2 is a time-shifted copy of column +1.
D4': if c_t=1 then a(t+1,-1) = a(t,1) OR a(t,2).
D5: if c_t=1 then a(t+1,1) = 1 XOR (a(t,1) OR a(t,2)).
Consequence of D1 and D4': column -1 is identically 1 on an alternating stretch exactly when (a(t,1), a(t,2)) is never (0,0) at a 1-phase in it.

Condrey 2026 Cor. 5 (primary source read): no column of a nonzero finite Rule 30 orbit is eventually constant. This is the theorem that would finish any argument reaching an eventually constant column.

Condrey Lemma 1 (triangular uniqueness): a prescribed trace plus a right half determines the left half uniquely. The alternating fiber therefore has exactly one left half per right half, like the constant fiber.
A finite horizon is evidence for designing a lemma, never a proof of one, and a finite-prefix violation does not refute an asymptotic lemma either.

obligations.lemma: If a nonzero finitely supported row has an eventually alternating centre trace, then column -1 is eventually identically 1.
obligations.implication: Excludes eventual period 2 (nonconstant) for every nonzero finite configuration, via Condrey Cor. 5: an eventually constant column is impossible. PARTIAL - every eventual period at least 3 remains open, so this is not Prize 1.
obligations.bridge: COMPLETE for p=2 and only for p=2. D1 already gives column -1 equal to 1 at every 1-phase, for free and independent of the right half. D4' turns the remaining half into a single condition: (a(t,1), a(t,2)) is never (0,0) at a 1-phase. So the lemma reduces to one sub-statement, and Condrey Cor. 5 finishes it in one line. Residue to reach all periods: p>=3, untouched, and no uniform argument over p is known.
obligations.missing_lemma: That (a(t,1), a(t,2)) != (0,0) at every large 1-phase, given the centre alternates forever and the row is finitely supported.
obligations.refutation: Among rows achieving the LONGEST alternating prefixes, does the double-zero event still occur at a 1-phase? If it persists at maximal prefix length the sub-lemma cannot come from local structure and must be derived from infinite alternation plus finite support.
obligations.falsifier_cost: Claude: under an hour. Compute: seconds, exhaustive over small support radius. Verification: exact enumeration against the repo's naive stepper.
obligations.stop: Stop if the double-zero event occurs at a 1-phase in rows with maximal alternating prefixes AND no finite-support ingredient can be identified, since then the sub-lemma has no visible mechanism.

mechanism_check.prize-restatement: This escapes the mechanism because it is a strictly partial exclusion, not an equivalent form: proving no finite row has an eventually alternating trace leaves every period at least 3 open, so it neither proves Prize 1 nor follows vacuously from Prize 1 being true.
mechanism_check.finite-exclusion-as-asymptotic: The enumeration is used only to design and stress the sub-lemma and is recorded as a bounded finding about small radius; the deliverable is a symbolic implication valid for all t, and a finite-prefix violation is explicitly not treated as a refutation.
mechanism_check.ensemble-not-orbit: Finitely supported configurations are a restricted class containing the lone seed rather than an average over initial conditions, and Condrey's Cor. 5 is proved for exactly that class.

obligations.lemma: For a prescribed right half, the unique left half compatible with an eventually alternating centre trace carries ones at arbitrarily large left depth, so no member is finitely supported.
obligations.implication: Excludes eventual period 2 (nonconstant) for every nonzero finite configuration, by exactly Condrey Cor. 4's argument. PARTIAL: every eventual period at least 3 remains open.
obligations.bridge: COMPLETE for p=2 and only for p=2, and it is the faithful transfer of the method that settles p=1. Condrey Lemma 1 already supplies uniqueness of the left half; what is missing is the closed form and the infinite-ones property. Residue to reach all periods: p>=3.
obligations.missing_lemma: The closed form of the alternating-trace left half, the analogue of Condrey's prefix-OR formulas, and the proof that every nonzero member has ones at arbitrarily large depth.
obligations.refutation: Compute the forced left half for many right halves and inspect its depth profile: a left half that terminates would refute the lemma outright.
obligations.falsifier_cost: Claude: days for the classification, which is out of scope this hour; the depth-profile probe alone is minutes. Verification: exact inversion checked against forward simulation.
obligations.stop: Stop if any forced left half terminates. Do not begin the full classification inside a one-hour block.

mechanism_check.prize-restatement: Partial exclusion, not an equivalent form: p>=3 is untouched, so it neither proves nor is vacuously implied by Prize 1.
mechanism_check.algebra-already-gives-it: Left permutivity gives uniqueness of the left half and nothing more; the closed form and the infinite-ones property are exactly what permutivity does not supply, which is why Condrey needed separate theorems for the constant case.
mechanism_check.finite-exclusion-as-asymptotic: The deliverable is a classification valid at every depth, and the depth probe is recorded as a bounded finding used to design it.

obligations.lemma: D3 extends: under an alternating centre trace, column -(k+1) is a time-shifted function of column k for every k, so the left half-plane is a reflection of the right.
obligations.implication: NONE directly, filed honestly as prize 'none'. It would make the left half explicit in terms of the right, which is the input alternating-fiber-support needs and which left-column-constant could use to control the double-zero event.
obligations.bridge: EXPLICITLY MISSING. A structural collapse is not an exclusion; on its own it yields no contradiction with finite support.
obligations.missing_lemma: Whether the D3 pattern continues past depth 2, and in what shifted form.
obligations.refutation: Check a(t,-3) against column 2 and a(t,-4) against column 3 on rows with long alternating prefixes. One mismatch kills the general form.
obligations.falsifier_cost: Claude: minutes. Compute: seconds, same enumeration already written. Verification: exact.
obligations.stop: Stop at the first depth where no shifted identity holds; record the depth reached as the bounded finding.

mechanism_check.algebra-already-gives-it: Sideways determinism gives that the left half is determined, but not that it is a reflection of the right half in this shifted form; D3 at depth 2 was derived and checked here rather than quoted.
mechanism_check.disjoint-from-prize-object: The columns are those of the same single orbit whose centre trace is hypothesised alternating, so the object intersects the prize object rather than sitting in the cone's settled wedge.

obligations.lemma: D1 forces ones at density at least one half in column -1, and that density propagates into a growing family of left columns, contradicting finite support.
obligations.implication: Would exclude eventual period 2 (nonconstant) for finite configurations. PARTIAL: p>=3 remains.
obligations.bridge: EXPLICITLY MISSING. Ones at positive density in TIME in a column says nothing about SPATIAL support at time zero, and the step from one to the other is exactly what is absent.
obligations.missing_lemma: Any argument connecting temporal density in left columns to spatial extent of the support.
obligations.refutation: Measure one-density in columns -1 to -k on rows with long alternating prefixes; a density collapsing to zero with depth would kill it.
obligations.falsifier_cost: Claude: hours, with no technique. Compute: seconds. Verification: measurement only, which verifies itself and nothing else.
obligations.stop: Park unless the missing space-time step is supplied by another candidate.
